questions.question: When are regular production deployments scheduled?
questions.answer: Regular production deployments are scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 14:00 German local time [NL-22:S2].

sources.title: Software Change Approval
sources.heading: Deployment window
sources.text: Regular deployments take place on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 14:00 German local time. Emergency changes outside that window require incident lead approval and a retrospective review on the next working day.

sources.title: Working Hours and Availability
sources.heading: Collaboration
sources.text: Shared availability hours are Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 15:00 German local time. Individual part-time agreements take precedence. Working time must be recorded daily in the time-tracking system.

sources.title: Onboarding Process
sources.heading: Before joining
sources.text: People Operations opens an onboarding ticket at least five working days before the start date. The manager specifies the role, team and required applications. IT Operations initially provisions standard access only.

sources.title: Working Hours and Availability
sources.heading: Absence
sources.text: Planned absences are entered in the team calendar. In the event of illness, notify the manager before the usual start of work. This document does not specify the annual leave entitlement.

sources.title: Remote Work Policy
sources.heading: Allowance
sources.text: Up to three remote-working days per calendar week are permitted with manager agreement. Required team meetings on site take priority. Unused remote-working days cannot be carried over to the following week.

recorded_review.notes: Required claims are covered; no material unsupported addition identified in this review.

questions.question: How long are internal knowledge platform backups retained?
questions.answer: There is a disagreement between the documents regarding the retention period for internal knowledge platform backups. Document NL-24:S1 states that backups are retained for 60 calendar days, while document NL-23:S1 specifies a retention period of 30 calendar days. Both documents are marked as active and neither provides a precedence rule over the other. Therefore, a definitive answer must be confirmed with the system owner. [NL-23:S2, NL-24:S2]

required_claims.criterion: Both documents active with no precedence rule

questions.question: Who must approve a software subscription costing EUR 15 per month?
questions.answer: A software subscription costing EUR 15 per month is a recurring purchase, so it requires approval from Finance and IT Operations regardless of the amount [NL-25:S1].

sources.title: Purchasing and Expenditure
sources.heading: Thresholds
sources.text: One-off purchases up to and including EUR 250 net require manager approval. Higher amounts also require Finance approval. Recurring software subscriptions require approval from Finance and IT Operations regardless of amount.

sources.title: Software Change Approval
sources.heading: Requirements
sources.text: A production change requires an approved pull request, successful automated checks and a documented rollback option. The author of the code must not be its sole approver.

sources.title: Purchasing and Expenditure
sources.heading: Ordering
sources.text: Place orders only after approval. Personal advance payments do not create an automatic right to reimbursement. Business travel is governed separately by documents NL-09, NL-11 and NL-12.

sources.title: Business Travel Process
sources.heading: Travel request
sources.text: Every business trip requires manager approval in the service portal before booking. The request must include purpose, dates, destination and estimated total cost. Any hotel rate above the limit must be explicitly identified.

sources.title: Expense Claim Procedure
sources.heading: Submission
sources.text: Each expense requires the date, amount, currency, category and a digital receipt. The submission deadline is defined by the current Travel Expense Policy. Credit card statements do not replace individual receipts.

sources.title: Working from Abroad
sources.heading: Workation
sources.text: Workation is permitted only within the EU for a maximum of ten working days per calendar year. Requests must be submitted at least 15 working days before the start date. Approval is not guaranteed.

sources.title: Remote Work Policy
sources.heading: Allowance
sources.text: Up to three remote-working days per calendar week are permitted with manager agreement. Required team meetings on site take priority. Unused remote-working days cannot be carried over to the following week.

sources.title: Access Requests
sources.heading: Time limits
sources.text: Administrator privileges are granted for no more than seven calendar days and require a new request afterwards. Shared user accounts are prohibited. Standard access is disabled at 18:00 German local time on the final working day when an employee leaves.

sources.title: Travel Expense Policy
sources.heading: Hotel costs
sources.text: For business travel within Germany, the standard hotel limit is EUR 120 gross per night, including breakfast. A higher rate requires written manager approval before booking. Document NL-11 also applies during trade fairs.
